heuristics.name: shared-function-random-mapping
heuristics.statement: Posited exploration law for one fixed r=64 r-adding walk (Montgomery-form-x partitions) with uniform table and wrapping residues from P uniform starts: (i) pooled birthday P(no collision) <= exp(-(63/64)T'(T'-1)/2q) charging only distinct-partition pairs; (ii) single-walk self-collision <= L^2/2q; (iii) distinguished indicators independent Bernoulli(2^-32) and bucket bits [38,137) i.i.d. uniform across distinct exploration points, with the distinguished window [6,38) disjoint from partition bits [0,6) by construction; (iv) solved-collision degeneracy <= 1/q + 2^-100 via the residue-mixing posit.
heuristics.support: Teske large-r analysis/experiments (uniform-table wrapping regime), Harris quantitative form, van Oorschot-Wiener pooling model, 112-bit record computation (Bos et al.) validating the birthday constant, same-regime toys incl. measured db uniformity (chi-square 19.89/24df); C0=0.65 sizes for modeled 0.4775 vs claimed 0.3995 (19% margin), absorbing constant-factor error. Bounded sampling cutoffs; exceptional path specified with E*=2^20 cap; abort analysis rigorous given the posit. No hash function or hash heuristic exists.

limitations: Analytic construction; no full-size execution or independent qualification.
Success relies on the supported multi-walk random-mapping heuristic.
Instruction budgets are conservative analytic upper bounds, not measured assembly.
The 2^98-entry table is an analytic device, as is the baseline's larger table.
Beats the generic BSGS control via batched parallel rho at the 0.39 threshold; not novel cryptanalysis.
Supersedes v14: disjoint distinguished window [6,38), corrected degeneracy 1/q + 2^-100, mixing posit with measured db uniformity, specified exceptional path with work cap; claim 129.20.
